text:
sam: Observed steady GPU memory growth on long-context evals with paged KV on H100. Runs leak ~200MB per 1k tokens, A100 doesn't show it. Logs point at repeated pt-walk spikes and evict queues not draining.
nina: yikes. repro script?
sam: small repro: run longctx_perf.py with --model paged-attn-2. snippet:
```
python longctx_perf.py --tokens 20000 --batch 1 --device h100 --kv-mode paged
```
We'll hit OOM after ~120k tokens on a single GPU.
omar: can you paste the nvprof / CUPTI sample? curious if kernels are getting stuck or if it's metadata buildup.
sam: attaching minimal trace excerpt:
```
[trace] pt_walk_ms: 1.2 0.9 1.1 12.6 13.0 12.9 0.8 0.9 13.1 13.2 ...
[evict] queue_len: 0 0 0 3 4 5 6 6 7 8
```
ryan: those 12-13ms spikes correspond to pt-walks that align with cache misses. The evict queue should drain but queue_len rising suggests evict worker isn't keeping up. Could be fragmentation causing many small pages to be freed individually.
nina: did we recently change coalescing heuristics? I remember a PR changed bitmap merge thresholds.
omar: yep PR #4823 bumped COALESCE_THRESHOLD from 8->16 to favour reuse. That reduces splitting but may leave more small free runs if page allocation/retire is asymmetric.
sam: confirmed: reverting coalesce threshold to 8 in debug build stops growth in a quick run. Not a final fix but suggests coalescing bug.
perf-bot: perf-regression alert: commit 9a7f1e2 increased tail latency for paged-pt by +22% on H100 in nightly.
ryan: ack. hypothesis: the new coalesce lowers immediate allocation churn but increases fragmentation pattern where reclaim path walks many tiny holes -> more pt-walk work and evict backlog. On H100 the kernel concurrency scheduling penalises many small evict ops vs a few larger ones; A100 scheduler behaves differently so you don't see regressions there.
nina: any repro artifacts? heap maps? run with REDWOOD_KV_DEBUG=1 to get page bitmap dumps.
sam: ran with that, here's snippet of free bitmap after 50k tokens:
```
free_runs: [512, 1, 1, 1024, 2, 1, 1, 1, 2048, 1, ...]
```
Huge number of length-1 runs.
omar: that's the ghost-page pattern. Our spill-merger didn't stitch adjacent singletons due to a bug when the adjacent owners moved across GPU ID boundaries. The merge checks were comparing owner_id != -1 but we use a packed owner where high bits encode migration flags; mask was wrong.
ryan: nice find. So the combo of changed threshold + packing bug produced runaway fragmentation on some MIG/hybrid setups.
sam: quick patch: mask owner_id with OWNER_MASK before comparison. With that the free_run histogram collapses and evict queue drains. Need thorough test.
nina: can you open a minimal unit test? also run on H100 perf infra. Add a synthetic that alternates owner flags to reproduce.
omar: working on a test now. Also will add an assert in pagetable::merge to catch mismasked owners in debug builds.
perf-bot: scheduling perf run on h100-nightly/kv-paged with patched merge. ETA ~2h.
ryan: other mitigation in runtime: increase evict worker batch_size to amortise per-evict kernel launch overhead on H100. Set default to 16 for h100 profiles until fix lands.
sam: doing that in a follow-up CL. Also adding metric for avg_free_run_length so we can alert earlier.
nina: sounds good. Create PRs: (1) mask owner fix + unit test, (2) revert coalesce threshold tweak + comment, (3) temp increase evict batch on h100. Link them in thread.
omar: PRs created: #4901 (#1), #4902 (#2), #4903 (#3). Running CI.
sam: thanks all. if perf run looks good we can backport to stable. I'll keep thread updated.
ryan: can someone add a short note to the release notes about the H100-specific behavior and the mitigation? ops needs heads-up.
nina: added to internal changelog.
sam: marking this resolved-for-now; will reopen if nightly shows recurrence. :thumbsup:
